clue.text: Certain police force caught in the act

indicators.note: something caught in another thing is held inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a deed is an act
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: Police officers arrest someone red-handed and feel sure of their case.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sure of a view is settled in their mind about it, having made up their mind.

clue.text: Carelessly draw fault in robot bomb

parts.note: to doodle is to scribble idly
a bug is a defect

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a flaw in a missile.
explanation.walkthrough: The V-1 flying bomb of the Second World War was nicknamed this in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The wartime nickname of the V-1, a pilotless flying bomb.

clue.text: Cheerful person making approach, perhaps

explanation.surface: A happy fellow coming forward.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf an approach shot to the green is often a chip.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively and bright; and a golfer who plays a short lofted shot to the green.

clue.text: Key is provided for drug supplier

parts.note: keys are pressed with the fingers, and digital relates to fingers or keys

explanation.surface: A key is given to a drug dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: The foxglove is the source of the heart drug digitalis.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxglove, whose leaves yield a heart medicine.

clue.text: Avoid nothing in military transport

explanation.surface: Someone avoids empty army vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: to dodge; a score of nothing in cricket; and the DUKW amphibious truck of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge; a batsman's zero in cricket; and the nickname of the wartime amphibious truck.

clue.text: Father's dancing in place of uncle

definitions.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, with the possessive S kept
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Dad is out on the dance floor at a relative's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker, so his place is the pawnshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a pawnbroker's premises, where goods are left in pledge for a loan.

clue.text: Author has to compete against one who had flying start

parts.note: to play is to take part, to compete
the Wright brothers made the first powered flight

explanation.surface: A writer competes with an aviation pioneer.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilbur and Orville Wright made the first powered aeroplane flight in 1903.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of dramas for the stage.

clue.text: Quietly polish ring

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for softly
to hone is to sharpen or refine

explanation.surface: Gently polishing a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like jewellery; it means to call.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is to call them on the telephone.

clue.text: Tormented ring-leader that's in difficult situation

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word for difficult

parts.note: hard describes a tough, difficult state of affairs

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: i.e. is id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A gang boss is tortured when caught in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring-leader' looks like a gang boss, but it gives only its first letter; 'in' sets that and the Latin abbreviation for 'that is' inside the word for difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Harassed and worried, pestered repeatedly.

clue.text: In confusion, follow stray animal

parts.note: pi is printers' jumbled type, a confusion of letters
to dog is to follow closely

explanation.surface: A muddled person trails a wandering creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Pi (also pie) is a printers' term for type that has been jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah dog, a stray ownerless mongrel of Asia.

clue.text: Outstanding all-rounder and football player

parts.note: O is round, a letter shaped like a ring
a wing is a winger, a wide attacking player

explanation.surface: Praise for a team's star versatile cricketer and footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All-rounder' suggests a sporting star, but here it is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt still unpaid is outstanding, due to be settled.

clue.text: Came with loud disturbance? That's about right

definitions.text: Came with loud disturbance? That's about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the other piece
a disturbance throws things into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rowdy arrival is described, with a wry comment that this sounds correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' jumbles the clue's first word with 'loud' into CLAMOUED, and 'about' wraps that round R. Read whole, the clue also describes a noisy arrival, so it is an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a loud outcry or noisy demand, as a crowd arriving with a din would.

clue.text: The French established a fantastic island

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
put can mean set or established in place

explanation.surface: A French group founded a remarkable island.
explanation.walkthrough: The flying island in Swift's Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: The floating island visited by Gulliver in Swift's satire, an imaginary land.

clue.text: Comprehensive school's head showing distress

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: weeping is crying, a show of distress

explanation.surface: A headteacher at a comprehensive is seen in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British state secondary school, which is the surface sense; here it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide-ranging, covering everything, as in sweeping changes.

clue.text: Taking off tapestries for repair

indicators.note: something in for repair gets taken apart and reassembled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wall hangings are removed to be mended.
explanation.definitionFit: An erotic act of removing clothes one by one.

clue.text: Gem taken in robbery located

indicators.note: taken in means contained within the following words

explanation.surface: A jewel stolen in a heist has been found.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious stone, the mineral family that includes emerald and aquamarine.

clue.text: Last person one would expect to take interest in Siam

parts.note: Tai is the people and language family of Siam, the old name for Thailand

parts.words: one would expect to take interest
parts.note: a lender is someone who charges interest on a loan

explanation.surface: Someone in Thailand is the least likely to be curious.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the last batsmen in the order are the weakest, the last people to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a weak batsman who comes in near the end of the order.

clue.text: Join volunteer force in harbour

parts.note: to enter is to join, as entering a profession
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Someone enlists in a reserve unit stationed at a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbour' looks like a port; it is the verb, as in harbour a hope.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold a thought or feeling in mind, to cherish it.

clue.text: Doctor sticks point right in the middle of back

indicators.note: sticks means is pushed in, placing the following pieces inside
in the middle of puts the pieces inside the word for back

parts.note: the rear is the back
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A medic plunges a needle right into the centre of a patient's back.
explanation.walkthrough: A registrar is a senior hospital doctor below consultant in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior hospital physician in training, ranking below a consultant.

clue.text: Versatile writer and craftsman

explanation.surface: A man of many talents, both an author and an artisan.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Goldsmith, the 18th-century Irish author, wrote poems, plays, a novel and essays.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver of that surname wrote poetry, drama and fiction; a worker in precious metal is a craftsman.

clue.text: Survive as most reluctant striker?

explanation.surface: Endure like the worker slowest to join a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: the last worker to come out on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure to the end; and the final worker to walk out.

clue.text: Object to bony scrag-end

parts.note: thin means lean, with bones showing

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone protests against a skinny cut of neck meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrag-end is the bony neck of mutton, a cheap British cut of meat. 'Object' looks like a verb; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An unnamed article or item is called a whatsit.

clue.text: Incentive provided after I'm dreadfully upset

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests things going badly wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A reward is offered after someone admits to being very distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadfully' shuffles UPSET into PETUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A driving force or stimulus.

clue.text: Be unwilling to incur loss, from what they say

definitions.text: incur loss, from what they say

explanation.surface: Someone holds back, fearing they will lose out, as the saying goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'he who hesitates is lost' supplies the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To falter or hang back; and in the proverb, whoever does so is lost.

clue.text: Suddenly upped and went for tramp

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly raised prices and went on a long walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised sharply, as of prices; and walked far in the country.

clue.text: Sign you need to know up North

parts.note: ken is a Scottish and northern English word for know

explanation.surface: A sign one must understand in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol or mark that stands for something.

clue.text: Sport I abandoned for final test

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A student gives up games to sit their exams.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is of SPORT and I. Cambridge University final honours exams have this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cambridge honours degree examination, taken at the end of a course.

clue.text: Conclusions of this work are somehow biased

indicators.note: conclusions are endings, so take the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: The findings of this study are skewed in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanted, distorted to one side.

clue.text: Disconcert champion after the innings

indicators.note: after places the word for champion behind the word for innings

parts.note: a knock is a cricketer's innings
to back is to support, to champion

explanation.surface: A star batsman is unsettled after a long stay at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman's innings is called a knock.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken aback or shocked, a setback.

clue.text: Poet heading this flower is belittled

definitions.text: Poet heading this flower is belittled

parts.words: Poet heading this flower is belittled
parts.note: put the word poet in front of the flower's name and the result is a sneering term for a bad versifier

explanation.surface: A flower is mocked when a poet stands before it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'flower'; a third-rate poet is called a poetaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like garden plant, Michaelmas daisy among them.

clue.text: Sweetheart married on the rebound, in this case

indicators.note: something on the rebound bounces back, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: united means joined in marriage
the heart of sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A lover weds someone new just after a break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rebound' turns UNITED into DETINU. 'case' is a legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit for recovery of goods wrongfully kept is a legal action.

clue.text: Get medal presented by king in royal house

parts.note: to win is to get or gain
the DSO is the Distinguished Service Order
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch awards a decoration in a palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The family name of the British royal dynasty since 1917.
